## Class

**17 `cleanup_comment_echo_jira.CleanupError: artifact directory must not be group/world
accessible: C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\…`** in job `100874330553`, concentrated in
`tests/integration/test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py` (19 failures, the 4th-largest file), plus
`st_mode` / `chmod(0o755)` / `S_IEXEC | S_IRWXU` assertion sites elsewhere in the log.

Windows has no POSIX mode bits. `os.chmod` accepts the call and silently applies only the read-only
attribute; `lstat().st_mode` then reports a value that never satisfies a
"not group/world accessible" test. The permission model is ACL-based, so the *intent* — "this
artifact directory is not readable by other principals" — is expressible, but not through mode bits.

## What the fix must decide

The check is a real security property, not a test artifact, so it must not simply be skipped. Two
defensible shapes:

- Express the intent per platform: mode-bit check on POSIX, an ACL check
  (`icacls` / `win32security`) on Windows.
- Or declare and document that the artifact-directory confidentiality guarantee is POSIX-only, make
  the production code say so at the call site, and mark the tests `skipif` with that reason cited —
  which is a real reduction in the Windows guarantee and must be recorded in the ADR's consequences.

Pick one deliberately. Do not let it default to whichever is easier.

## Blocked by S1

## Proving command

```
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/integration/test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py \
  -p no:cacheprovider -q
```
on `windows-latest`, plus a whole-sweep check:
```
uv run --no-sync pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 \
  | grep -cE "must not be group/world accessible|st_mode"   # must be 0
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. Zero mode-bit-derived failures in a Windows sweep.
2. Whichever shape is chosen, the artifact-confidentiality guarantee's platform scope is stated in
   the production code at the enforcing call site, not only in a test.
